scope: IELTS Academic Speaking, one answer to one question (Part 1, 2 or 3)

source.name: IELTS Speaking Band Descriptors, public version
source.descriptor_version: PDF created 16 September 2025 (no version number printed)
source.note: Each band entry below is a paraphrased summary written by the team, not a verbatim copy of the official descriptors. Bands 0-2 are condensed into 'floor_rules'.

scoring_notes: Each criterion is scored as an integer 0-9. A response should fit the positive features of a band to receive it; a clear weakness described at a lower band caps the score.

The official descriptors rate a candidate on the average performance across all parts of the test. Here a single answer is scored, so the result is only an estimate for learning, not an official IELTS result.
The grader sees a machine transcript and numbers, not the audio. Pronunciation is judged from the pronunciation scores; without them the band is only an indirect estimate.
Calibration range is band 4-8; results outside it are flagged out_of_calibration_range.

expected_length.QT_S_PART1: A short, direct answer of about 2-4 sentences.
expected_length.QT_S_PART2: A long turn of about 1-2 minutes that covers the points on the cue card.
expected_length.QT_S_PART3: An extended answer that gives reasons, comparisons or examples.

floor_rules.band_2: Long pauses before almost every word; only isolated words or memorised phrases; speech carries almost no meaning.
floor_rules.band_1: No rateable language except a few isolated words; nothing can be understood.
floor_rules.band_0: Did not attend or did not complete the test; for a single answer, also no speech at all.

CRIT_S_FC.name: Fluency and Coherence
CRIT_S_FC.focus: Keeps speaking at a natural pace, develops the answer, and links ideas clearly.

bands.9: Speaks fluently; repetition or self-correction is very rare; any hesitation is for planning content, not for finding words; ideas fully developed and coherent.
bands.8: Fluent, with very rare repetition or self-correction; hesitation is mostly about content, with only occasional word-finding pauses; development is coherent and relevant.
bands.7: Keeps going and produces long turns without visible effort; some hesitation, repetition or self-correction, often mid-sentence, shows trouble finding language but does not harm coherence; discourse markers and connectives used flexibly.
bands.6: Willing to give long turns; coherence is sometimes lost through hesitation, repetition or self-correction; uses a range of connectives and discourse markers, not always appropriately.
bands.5: Usually keeps going but leans on repetition, self-correction or slow speech; pauses often come while searching for basic words; some linking words are overused; harder content breaks the flow while simple content can be fluent.
bands.4: Cannot continue without noticeable pauses; slow, repeats itself and often corrects itself; joins simple sentences with repetitive connectives; coherence sometimes breaks down.
bands.3: Frequent and sometimes long pauses while searching for words; little ability to link sentences or go beyond simple answers; often cannot get the basic message across.

CRIT_S_LR.name: Lexical Resource
CRIT_S_LR.focus: Range, precision and naturalness of vocabulary, including paraphrasing.

bands.9: Total flexibility and precision in every context; accurate, idiomatic language sustained throughout.
bands.8: Wide vocabulary used readily and flexibly for all topics; skilful use of less common and idiomatic items despite occasional slips in word choice or collocation; paraphrases effectively.
bands.7: Vocabulary used flexibly across a variety of topics; some less common and idiomatic items with awareness of style and collocation, though inappropriate uses occur; paraphrases effectively.
bands.6: Enough vocabulary to discuss topics at length; some word choices are inappropriate but the meaning stays clear; generally paraphrases successfully.
bands.5: Enough vocabulary for familiar and unfamiliar topics but with little flexibility; tries to paraphrase with mixed success.
bands.4: Enough for familiar topics, but only basic meaning on unfamiliar ones; frequent inappropriate or wrong word choices; rarely tries to paraphrase.
bands.3: Only simple words, mostly for personal information; vocabulary is inadequate for unfamiliar topics.

CRIT_S_GRA.name: Grammatical Range and Accuracy
CRIT_S_GRA.focus: Variety of sentence structures and how accurately they are used.

bands.9: Structures precise and accurate at all times, apart from slips typical of native speech.
bands.8: Wide range of structures used flexibly; most sentences are error-free; only occasional non-systematic errors, and a few basic errors may persist.
bands.7: A range of structures used flexibly; error-free sentences are frequent; simple and complex sentences both work despite some errors, and a few basic errors persist.
bands.6: Mix of short and complex sentences and a variety of structures with limited flexibility; complex structures often contain errors, but these rarely get in the way of meaning.
bands.5: Basic sentence forms are fairly accurate; complex structures are tried but limited in range, nearly always faulty, and may need rephrasing.
bands.4: Basic forms only, and some short utterances are error-free; subordinate clauses are rare, turns are short, structures repeat and errors are frequent.
bands.3: Basic forms are attempted but errors are numerous, except in memorised phrases.

CRIT_S_P.name: Pronunciation
CRIT_S_P.focus: Clarity and control of sounds, stress, rhythm and intonation. Judged from the pronunciation scores, because the transcript carries no sound.

bands.9: Full range of features used to convey fine meaning, sustained; effortless to understand; accent does not affect intelligibility.
bands.8: Wide range of features; keeps an appropriate rhythm and uses stress and intonation flexibly over long stretches despite occasional lapses; easy to understand; accent has minimal effect.
bands.7: Shows the positive features of band 6 and some, but not all, of band 8.
bands.6: Uses a range of features with variable control; chunking is mostly appropriate but rhythm can suffer; stress and intonation are not sustained; some words or sounds are mispronounced but clarity is only occasionally lost; generally understood without much effort.
bands.5: Shows the positive features of band 4 and some, but not all, of band 6.
bands.4: Some acceptable features but limited range; frequent lapses in rhythm; limited control of stress and intonation; words and sounds are often mispronounced, so understanding takes effort and some stretches cannot be understood.
bands.3: Shows some features of band 2 and some, but not all, of band 4.

score_hints.note: Hints for reading the Azure pronunciation scores (0-100). They are rough guides written by the team, not part of the official descriptors, and must be checked on real samples before they are relied on.
score_hints.accuracy: Main basis for how clear the sounds are.
score_hints.fluency: Second opinion for rhythm and pauses; never the only reason for a band.
score_hints.prosody: Main basis for stress, intonation and rhythm; may be null.
score_hints.completeness: A low value may mean words were skipped or not recognised.
